findings.title: Harmful-habit claims omit required provenance and stale-signal demotion
findings.what: The recommendation asserts that a habit tracks with worse outcomes and reports rates, magnitude, affected sessions, and total sessions, but returns only free-form evidence at lines 82-99. It supplies no provenance observations identifying the source fields and no asOf/stale metadata, so an old corpus is still presented as a current relationship.
findings.fix: Add structured observations for the factor key, high/low counts and good rates, document the proxy inference, derive the latest supporting session date, and prefix stale detail with "As of <date>" while setting provenance.asOf and provenance.stale.
findings.acceptance: A detector test validates recommendation provenance and proves that a corpus older than the freshness threshold emits detail beginning "As of YYYY-MM-DD," with matching provenance.asOf and stale=true; fresh data remains undemoted.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed the return object at src/lib/detectors/workflow/harmful-habit.ts:78-100 ends after evidence and contains neither provenance nor any date/freshness calculation. The existing test only checks that evidence is non-empty.

findings.title: Span sizing repeatedly scans all token entries for each span
findings.what: spanTokenPoolsFor iterates a session's token rows from the beginning for every steering span (lines 191-216), and rule calls it once per span at lines 353-370. For S spans sharing a session with T token entries this is O(S×T), despite rows already being timestamp-sorted.
findings.fix: Build per-session prefix sums for the four token pools and use binary searches for each span's start/end indices, reducing each span query to O(log T).
findings.acceptance: Add a multi-span performance probe with at least 1,000 spans and 100,000 token entries in one session; verify token totals are unchanged and entry visits/query work scale near O(T + S log T), not O(S×T).
findings.verifyNote: Second pass re-read confirmed tokenEntriesBySession sorts rows at src/lib/detectors/workflow/human-input-leverage.ts:173-189, but spanTokenPoolsFor at lines 191-216 linearly rescans them and is invoked inside the per-span map at lines 353-370. No indexed range query or scan cursor is used.

findings.title: Low-tool-effectiveness recommendation lacks structured provenance and freshness
findings.what: The detector claims a tool is persistently ineffective from a composite score and invocation count, but lines 29-60 emit only formatted evidence. They do not identify the underlying artifact fields or inference in structured provenance, and no timestamps are carried forward to demote historical results.
findings.fix: Attach provenance observations for tool identity, invocation count, effectiveness score, and the constituent error/undo/retry/forward-motion fields; derive the latest contributing event date and mark stale output as of that date.
findings.acceptance: A test validates the emitted provenance structure and demonstrates that an old tool corpus is worded "As of <date>" with provenance.asOf/stale, while a fresh corpus preserves current wording.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read of src/lib/detectors/workflow/low-tool-effectiveness.ts:21-60 confirmed the calculation output includes evidence and an illustrative fix but no provenance, timestamp selection, asOf, or stale field. The dispatched test asserts only firing and suppression.

findings.title: Mid-turn interruption history is always presented as current
findings.what: Each interrupt retains interruptTs, but the rollup discards temporal context and emits present-tense detail at lines 183-203. The rule does not use its now argument or set provenance.asOf/stale, so arbitrarily old interruptions remain an undated current recommendation.
findings.fix: Compute the latest valid interruptTs, compare it with a documented freshness threshold using the detector's now argument, prefix stale detail with "As of <date>", and add provenance.asOf/stale.
findings.acceptance: A test using three old interrupts verifies detail begins "As of YYYY-MM-DD," and provenance reports the same date with stale=true; a corresponding fresh fixture reports stale=false without the prefix.
findings.verifyNote: Second pass confirmed interruptTs is captured at src/lib/detectors/workflow/mid-turn-interrupt-steering.ts:111-116, but the rule signature at line 132 ignores now and the returned provenance at lines 199-203 contains only observations and inference.

findings.title: Each interrupt rescans the session's full token history
findings.what: wastedInWindow loops over all token entries, and collectSessionInterrupts invokes it separately for every qualifying interrupt. A session with I interrupts and T token entries therefore performs O(I×T) parsing and pricing work on the detector hot path.
findings.fix: Sort/index token entries once per session and advance a monotonic cursor alongside timeline traversal, or use timestamp binary searches plus prefix sums for output tokens and per-model cost.
findings.acceptance: A performance probe with many interrupts and token entries shows unchanged wasted-token/dollar results while token-entry processing scales linearly or O((I+T) log T), with no full rescan per interrupt.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed the full token loop at src/lib/detectors/workflow/mid-turn-interrupt-steering.ts:63-69 is called from the interrupt branch at lines 107-116. The advancing boundary prevents double counting but does not prevent repeated scans.
